----- all constraints satisfied — score optimality -----------------\n        actual_sum = sum(x)\n        if actual_sum == optimal_sum:\n            return 1.0\n\n        # Sub-optimal: score decays with excess over optimum.\n        excess = actual_sum - optimal_sum\n        score = max(0.0, 1.0 - excess / optimal_sum)\n        return float(score)\n","numLines":246,"startLine":1,"totalLines":246}}}

We use Docker:\n    35→\n    36→```bash\n    37→# Pull the image\n    38→docker pull slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126\n    39→\n    40→# Start the container\n    41→docker run -d --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \\\n    42→  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \\\n    43→  --name RLVE \\\n    44→  slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126 \\\n    45→  tail -f /dev/null\n    46→```\n    47→\n    48→After entering the Docker container, please follow these steps to clone the repository and install it:\n    49→\n    50→```bash\n    51→cd /root/\n    52→git clone https://github.com/Zhiyuan-Zeng/RLVE.git\n    53→cd RLVE\n    54→pip install -e .\n    55→```\n    56→\n    57→## Usage of Verifiable Environments in RLVE-Gym\n    58→\n    59→Each environment has an identifier, which you can find [here](Gym/environments/__init__.py). We take the following example:\n    60→\n    61→```python\n    62→identifier = \"Sorting\"\n    63→```\n    64→\n    65→Each environment has two classes - one for the environment itself and another for controlling the problem difficulty:\n    66→\n    67→```python\n    68→from Gym.environments import identifier2environment\n    69→from Gym.parameter_controllers import identifier2controller\n    70→\n    71→environment = identifier2environment[identifier]\n    72→controller_class = identifier2controller[identifier]\n    73→```\n    74→\n    75→Note that when creating the environment, you can specify the argument `answer_markers` to control how the answer is extracted from a model’s output during verification.\n    76→By default, it extracts the answer enclosed between `<answer>` and `</answer>`.\n    77→You can check [this example usage](slime/rollout/rm_hub/rlve_rm.py) for reference.\n    78→\n    79→When generating a problem, we specify a random seed `seed` and a problem difficulty level `d` ($d \\geq 0$):\n    80→\n    81→```python\n    82→import random\n    83→\n    84→seed = 42\n    85→\n    86→controller = controller_class()\n    87→d = 3\n    88→for _ in range(d) :\n    89→    controller.update()\n    90→\n    91→problem = environment()\n    92→parameter = random.choice(controller.get_parameter_list())\n    93→if problem.generator(seed = seed, parameter = parameter) :\n    94→    pass\n    95→else :\n    96→    problem = None\n    97→```\n    98→\n    99→Problem generation is successful when `problem` is not `None`.\n   100→\n   101→The input prompt is obtained via `problem.prompt_generator()`.  \n   102→The reward for a model output `output` is given by `problem.scorer(output)`, or you can access more detailed verification information using `problem.verifier(output)`.\n   103→\n   104→You can check [here](Gym/environment.py) for more detailed usage.\n   105→\n   106→## Model Download & Weight Conversion\n   107→\n   108→In the following, model will be trained from randomly initialized weights.\n   157→\n   158→\n   159→## Reward Shaping\n   160→\n   161→By default, we use the original reward provided by each verifiable environment as the reward used in the RL algorithm.  \n   162→Many environments employ continuous reward shaping, meaning that a model output can still receive a positive reward even if its answer is not fully correct.  \n   163→We found that when the training scale is small, using a binary reward can sometimes yield slightly better results (i.e., the model output receives 1 if and only if its answer is fully correct, and 0 otherwise).  \n   164→You can switch to binary rewards by changing `--reward-key reward` to `--reward-key accuracy` in `scripts/training/[MODEL]/rlve.sh`.\n   165→\n   166→## When reporting a problem, provide detailed information so we can assist you more effectively.\n\n## Setup\n\nOur environment setup is the same as the setup of the official [slime](https://github.com/THUDM/slime) framework. We use Docker:\n\n```bash\n# Pull the image\ndocker pull slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126\n\n# Start the container\ndocker run -d --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \\\n  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \\\n  --name RLVE \\\n  slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126 \\\n  tail -f /dev/null\n```\n\nAfter entering the Docker container, please follow these steps to clone the repository and install it:\n\n```bash\ncd /root/\ngit clone https://github.com/Zhiyuan-Zeng/RLVE.git\ncd RLVE\npip install -e .\n```\n\n## Usage of Verifiable Environments in RLVE-Gym\n\nEach environment has an identifier, which you can find [here](Gym/environments/__init__.py). We take the following example:\n\n```python\nidentifier = \"Sorting\"\n```\n\nEach environment has two classes - one for the environment itself and another for controlling the problem difficulty:\n\n```python\nfrom Gym.environments import identifier2environment\nfrom Gym.parameter_controllers import identifier2controller\n\nenvironment = identifier2environment[identifier]\ncontroller_class = identifier2controller[identifier]\n```\n\nNote that when creating the environment, you can specify the argument `answer_markers` to control how the answer is extracted from a model’s output during verification.\nBy default, it extracts the answer enclosed between `<answer>` and `</answer>`.\nYou can check [this example usage](slime/rollout/rm_hub/rlve_rm.py) for reference.\n\nWhen generating a problem, we specify a random seed `seed` and a problem difficulty level `d` ($d \\geq 0$):\n\n```python\nimport random\n\nseed = 42\n\ncontroller = controller_class()\nd = 3\nfor _ in range(d) :\n    controller.update()\n\nproblem = environment()\nparameter = random.choice(controller.get_parameter_list())\nif problem.generator(seed = seed, parameter = parameter) :\n    pass\nelse :\n    problem = None\n```\n\nProblem generation is successful when `problem` is not `None`.\n\nThe input prompt is obtained via `problem.prompt_generator()`.  \nThe reward for a model output `output` is given by `problem.scorer(output)`, or you can access more detailed verification information using `problem.verifier(output)`.\n\nYou can check [here](Gym/environment.py) for more detailed usage.\n\n## Model Download & Weight Conversion\n\nIn the following, we assume you are on a node with 8 GPUs, each equipped with at least 80GB of memory.\nWe recommend using H100 or H200 GPUs over A100s, due to recent findings regarding floating-point precision issues observed on A100 hardware.\n\nWe download models from Hugging Face and convert their weights from the Hugging Face format to the Megatron format:\n\n```bash\n# Qwen2.5-7B-Base\nhf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B --local-dir ../Qwen2.5-7B\nsource scripts/models/qwen2.5-7B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../Qwen2.5-7B \\\n    --save ../Qwen2.5-7B_torch_dist\n\n# R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B\nhf download deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B --local-dir ../DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B\nsource scripts/models/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B \\\n    --save ../DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B_torch_dist\n\n# DeepScaleR-1.5B\nhf download agentica-org/DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview --local-dir ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview\nsource scripts/models/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview \\\n    --save ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview_torch_dist\n\n# ProRL-1.5B-v2\nhf download nvidia/Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B --revision v2 --local-dir ../Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B-v2\nsource scripts/models/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B-v2 \\\n    --save ../Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B-v2_torch_dist\n\n# OpenThinker3-1.5B\nhf download open-thoughts/OpenThinker3-1.5B --local-dir ../OpenThinker3-1.5B\nsource scripts/models/qwen2.5-1.5B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../OpenThinker3-1.5B \\\n    --save ../OpenThinker3-1.5B_torch_dist\n```\n\n**Warning:** Please make sure the weight conversion is successful before starting any training.\nEven if the conversion fails, training can still launch without a runtime error, but the model will be trained from randomly initialized weights.\n\n\n## Reward Shaping\n\nBy default, we use the original reward provided by each verifiable environment as the reward used in the RL algorithm.  \nMany environments employ continuous reward shaping, meaning that a model output can still receive a positive reward even if its answer is not fully correct.  \nWe found that when the training scale is small, using a binary reward can sometimes yield slightly better results (i.e., the model output receives 1 if and only if its answer is fully correct, and 0 otherwise).  \nYou can switch to binary rewards by changing `--reward-key reward` to `--reward-key accuracy` in `scripts/training/[MODEL]/rlve.sh`.\n\n## Wandb Setup\n\nTo use Weights & Biases (wandb), please set your wandb API key in the environment variable `WANDB_API_KEY`.  \nAlternatively, you can comment out the wandb-related arguments in `WANDB_ARGS` within the training script to disable wandb.\n\n## Environment Scaling\n\nYou can run our environment scaling experiments as follows:\n\n```bash\n# Qwen2.5-7B-Base\nbash The docstring and code define five reward tiers:\n\n```python\ndef scorer(self, output: str) -> float:\n    # ----- extract answer from raw output -----\n    answer = self._extract_answer(output)\n    parsed = self._process(answer)\n    if parsed is None:\n        return -1.0                      # unparseable -> -1.0\n\n    x = parsed\n    N = self.parameter['N']\n    constraints = self.parameter['constraints']\n    optimal_sum = self.parameter['optimal_sum']\n\n    # ----- positivity -----\n    pos_violations = sum(1 for v in x if v <= 0)\n    if pos_violations > 0:\n        return -1.0 + 0.5 * (pos_violations / N)   # [-1.0, -0.5]\n\n    # ----- constraint satisfaction -----\n    total_c = len(constraints)\n    c_violations = 0\n    for u, v, d, typ in constraints:\n        if typ == '=':\n            if x[v] - x[u] != d:\n                c_violations += 1\n        else:  # '>='\n            if x[v] - x[u] < d:\n                c_violations += 1\n\n    if c_violations > 0:\n        frac_satisfied = (total_c - c_violations) / total_c\n        return -0.5 + 0.5 * frac_satisfied          # (-0.5, 0.0]\n\n    # ----- all constraints satisfied — score optimality -----\n    actual_sum = sum(x)\n    if actual_sum == optimal_sum:\n        return 1.0                                  # optimal -> +1.0\n\n    excess = actual_sum - optimal_sum\n    score = max(0.0, 1.0 - excess / optimal_sum)    # [0.0, 1.0)\n    return float(score)\n```\n\nSo the reward ladder is:\n- **-1.0**: answer not parseable as N integers.\n- **[-1.0, -0.5]**: parsed, but some variables are non-positive (linear penalty per non-positive variable).\n- **(-0.5, 0.0]**: all positive, but some constraints violated (linear interpolation by fraction of satisfied constraints).\n- **[0.0, 1.0)**: all constraints satisfied, but sum is above the minimal `optimal_sum` (decays by relative excess).\n- **+1.0**: all constraints satisfied AND the sum equals the computed minimal sum (`optimal_solution`).\n\nThe `optimal_solution`/`optimal_sum` are computed in `_generate()` (lines 64-99) via a fixed-point relaxation starting from all-ones.\n\nThere is also an **unregistered** sibling controller for `difference_constraint_system` (non-DAG) at `/workspace/Gym/parameter_controllers/difference_constraint_system/parameter_controller.py` — identical logic to the DAG one — but no environment file exists for it; the only registered environment is the DAG variant.\n\n---\n\n### 2. The eval metric is therefore the **mean `scorer` score** over those 128 problems.\n\n> Note: in this workspace `Gym/environments/__init__.py` only registers `DifferenceConstraintSystemDAG`; the held-out names would need to be registered in the full Gym install for the historical run to work.\n\n---\n\n## 3. How rollout rewards are computed and logged\n\n### Reward assignment during generation\n\n`generate_and_rm` (`/workspace/slime/rollout/sglang_rollout.py`) assigns `sample.reward`:\n- Non-group RM: `sample.reward = await async_rm(args, sample)`.\n- Group RM: rewards assigned later in `generate_and_rm_group` via `batched_async_rm`.\n\n### Post-processing + GRPO normalization\n\n`RolloutController.generate` (`/workspace/slime/ray/buffer.py`) calls `post_process_rewards`, which does the **group-level normalization**:\n\n```python\nraw_rewards = [sample.get_reward_value(self.args) for sample in samples]\nif (self.args.advantage_estimator in [\"grpo\", \"gspo\", \"reinforce_plus_plus_baseline\"]\n        and self.args.rewards_normalization):\n    rewards = torch.tensor(raw_rewards, dtype=torch.float)\n    rewards = rewards.reshape(-1, self.args.n_samples_per_prompt)\n    mean = rewards.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n    rewards = rewards - mean                       # subtract group mean\n    if self.args.advantage_estimator in [\"grpo\", \"gspo\"] and self.args.grpo_std_normalization:\n        std = rewards.std(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n        rewards = rewards / (std + 1e-6)           # Dr. GRPO std normalization\n    return raw_rewards, rewards.flatten().tolist()\nreturn raw_rewards, raw_rewards\n```\n\nThe normalized `rewards` are stored in `train_data[\"rewards\"]` and `raw_rewards` in `train_data[\"raw_reward\"]` (`_convert_samples_to_train_data`).\n\n### Logging\n\n- During rollout: `log_rollout_data` in `/workspace/slime/ray/buffer.py` logs `perf/rollout_time`, `perf/tokens_per_gpu_per_sec`, `perf/longest_sample_tokens_per_sec`.\n- After training/advantage computation: `log_rollout_data` in `/workspace/slime/backends/megatron_utils/data.py` (lines 98-146) logs per-sample-mean values of `rewards`, `raw_reward`, `log_probs`, `ref_log_probs`, `returns`, `advantages`, `entropy`, etc., all under the `rollout/` prefix. How GRPO advantage estimation works\n\n### Reward normalization (already done in the rollout buffer, see above)\n\nThe group-normalized rewards become the \"rewards\" fed into the training actor.\n\n### Megatron backend — `/workspace/slime/backends/megatron_utils/loss.py`\n\n`compute_advantages_and_returns` (line 99):\n\n```python\nrewards = torch.tensor(rewards, dtype=torch.float32, device=kl[0].device)\n\nif args.advantage_estimator in [\"grpo\", \"gspo\"]:\n    returns = get_grpo_returns(rewards, kl)\n    advantages = [r for r in returns]\n...\nif args.normalize_advantages:\n    # distributed_masked_whiten over all advantages (global whiten)\n```\n\n`get_grpo_returns` (`/workspace/slime/utils/ppo_utils.py` line 124) broadcasts each sequence's scalar reward to every token:\n\n```python\ndef get_grpo_returns(rewards, kl):\n    returns = []\n    for i in range(len(rewards)):\n        returns.append(torch.ones_like(kl[i]) * rewards[i])\n    return returns\n```\n\nSo for GRPO, per-token advantage = normalized group reward (mean-subtracted, optionally std-divided), constant across the response. KL penalty is *not* baked into the GRPO advantage here — the optional `--use-kl-loss` path adds a separate KL loss term in `policy_loss_function` (line 279). How rollout rewards are computed and logged\n\n### Reward assignment during generation\n\n`generate_and_rm` (`/workspace/slime/rollout/sglang_rollout.py`) assigns `sample.reward`:\n- Non-group RM: `sample.reward = await async_rm(args, sample)`.\n- Group RM: rewards assigned later in `generate_and_rm_group` via `batched_async_rm`.\n\n### Post-processing + GRPO normalization\n\n`RolloutController.generate` (`/workspace/slime/ray/buffer.py`) calls `post_process_rewards`, which does the **group-level normalization**:\n\n```python\nraw_rewards = [sample.get_reward_value(self.args) for sample in samples]\nif (self.args.advantage_estimator in [\"grpo\", \"gspo\", \"reinforce_plus_plus_baseline\"]\n        and self.args.rewards_normalization):\n    rewards = torch.tensor(raw_rewards, dtype=torch.float)\n    rewards = rewards.reshape(-1, self.args.n_samples_per_prompt)\n    mean = rewards.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n    rewards = rewards - mean                       # subtract group mean\n    if self.args.advantage_estimator in [\"grpo\", \"gspo\"] and self.args.grpo_std_normalization:\n        std = rewards.std(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n        rewards = rewards / (std + 1e-6)           # Dr. GRPO std normalization\n    return raw_rewards, rewards.flatten().tolist()\nreturn raw_rewards, raw_rewards\n```\n\nThe normalized `rewards` are stored in `train_data[\"rewards\"]` and `raw_rewards` in `train_data[\"raw_reward\"]` (`_convert_samples_to_train_data`).\n\n### Logging\n\n- During rollout: `log_rollout_data` in `/workspace/slime/ray/buffer.py` logs `perf/rollout_time`, `perf/tokens_per_gpu_per_sec`, `perf/longest_sample_tokens_per_sec`.\n- After training/advantage computation: `log_rollout_data` in `/workspace/slime/backends/megatron_utils/data.py` (lines 98-146) logs per-sample-mean values of `rewards`, `raw_reward`, `log_probs`, `ref_log_probs`, `returns`, `advantages`, `entropy`, etc., all under the `rollout/` prefix. Optionally logs `passrate/*` via `log_passrate` (counts `raw_reward == 1` per group).\n\n---\n\n## 4. How GRPO advantage estimation works\n\n### Reward normalization (already done in the rollout buffer, see above)\n\nThe group-normalized rewards become the \"rewards\" fed into the training actor.\n\n### Megatron backend — `/workspace/slime/backends/megatron_utils/loss.py`\n\n`compute_advantages_and_returns` (line 99):\n\n```python\nrewards = torch.tensor(rewards, dtype=torch.float32, device=kl[0].device)\n\nif args.advantage_estimator in [\"grpo\", \"gspo\"]:\n    returns = get_grpo_returns(rewards, kl)\n    advantages = [r for r in returns]\n...\nif args.normalize_advantages:\n    # distributed_masked_whiten over all advantages (global whiten)\n```\n\n`get_grpo_returns` (`/workspace/slime/utils/ppo_utils.py` line 124) broadcasts each sequence's scalar reward to every token:\n\n```python\ndef get_grpo_returns(rewards, kl):\n    returns = []\n    for i in range(len(rewards)):\n        returns.append(torch.ones_like(kl[i]) * rewards[i])\n    return returns\n```\n\nSo for GRPO, per-token advantage = normalized group reward (mean-subtracted, optionally std-divided), constant across the response. KL penalty is *not* baked into the GRPO advantage here — the optional `--use-kl-loss` path adds a separate KL loss term in `policy_loss_function` (line 279). If `--normalize-advantages` is set, advantages are additionally globally whitened with `distributed_masked_whiten`.\n\n### FSDP backend — `/workspace/slime/backends/fsdp_utils/actor.py` (line 190)\n\n```python\nif self.args.advantage_estimator in [\"grpo\", \"gspo\"]:\n    batch[\"advantages\"] = batch[\"returns\"] = batch[\"rewards\"].expand_as(batch[\"log_probs\"])\n```\n\nSame idea — broadcast the scalar reward to all response tokens.\n\n### Loss\n\n`compute_policy_loss` (`/workspace/slime/utils/ppo_utils.py` line 48) computes the clipped PPO objective; `--use-tis` adds importance-sampling weights using `rollout_log_probs`.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What \"rlve\" rollout_global_dataset does differently\n\nBoth are mutually exclusive data sources (`/workspace/slime/ray/rollout_data_source.py` line 147):\n\n```python\nassert (args.rollout_global_dataset and not args.rlve) or (not args.rollout_global_dataset and args.rlve)\n```\n\n### Data source construction\n\n- **`rollout_global_dataset`**: loads a static `Dataset` from `args.prompt_data` (JSON/JSONL), applies chat template, and shuffles by epoch. `get_samples` returns deep-copied prompt samples grouped `n_samples_per_prompt` at a time, advancing `sample_offset`/`epoch_id`.\n- **`rlve`**: builds a `RLVEManager` (same file, lines 22-133) that **procedurally generates** problems from the `Gym` environments. Each `get_sample()`:\n  - picks a random environment from `args.environment_list`,\n  - draws a difficulty in the sliding window `[max_difficulty - difficulty_sliding_window_size, max_difficulty]`,\n  - instantiates the environment, calls `generator(seed, parameter)`, then `prompt_generator()`,\n  - stores `metadata = dict(environment=..., problem_difficulty=..., config=problem.get_config())`.\n\n`RolloutDataSource.get_samples` branches:\n- Standard: iterates `self.dataset.samples[...]`, creating `n_samples_per_prompt` copies per prompt.\n- RLVE: loops calling `rlve_manager.get_sample()` until it has `num_samples` groups, each with `n_samples_per_prompt` copies of the generated problem.\n\n### Rollout generation loop — `/workspace/slime/rollout/sglang_rollout.py`\n\nIn `generate_rollout_async`:\n- Standard mode: keeps only `data` (groups passing the optional `dynamic_filter`); unused samples are simply dropped.\n- **RLVE mode**: additionally requires `data_buffer.rlve_manager` and, after generation, calls:\n\n```python\nlog_dict = data_buffer.rlve_manager.update(samples=all_data)\n```\n\n`RLVEManager.update` (lines 101-133) updates per-environment accuracy from `sample.reward[\"accuracy\"]` (only for samples at max difficulty), and when `min_prompts_before_difficulty_check * n_samples_per_prompt` samples accumulate:\n- logs `RLVE/{environment}/accuracy`,\n- increments `environment2difficulty[environment]` when accuracy ≥ `min_metric_to_increase_difficulty`,\n- resets the accuracy counter.\n\nThese `RLVE/*` metrics are logged to wandb with `rollout/step` as the x-axis (`sglang_rollout.py` lines 322-336; `wandb_utils.py` line 128).\n\nSo the RLVE manager enables **adaptive curriculum learning**: problems get harder as the model's accuracy on an environment crosses a threshold.\n\n### Checkpointing\n\n`RolloutDataSource.save/load`:\n- `rollout_global_dataset` saves/loads `rollout/global_dataset_state_dict_{rollout_id}.pt` (sample_offset, epoch_id, sample_index, metadata).\n- `rlve` saves/loads `rollout/rlve_manager_state_dict_{rollout_id}.pt` (environment2difficulty, environment2accuracy, problem_generation_seed).\n\n---\n\n## Key files summary\n\n| Concern | File / functions |\n|---|---|\n| Eval trigger | `/workspace/train.py` (train loop),
